A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cache-selection approach, renamed from LongCache to ReAttention. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. All 11 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2 were inspected, including v2's Appendices A–B; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench, L-Eval, single- and multi-needle retrieval experiments, together with attention-distribution case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and retrieval results, efficiency measurements, hyperparameter ablations, RULER experiments and appendix cache-visualization analyses.

M1.justification: The selection, voting, neighboring-span extraction and positional-reassignment procedure in Sections 2.1–2.2 remains unchanged. However, v2 implements a fused Triton kernel for attention-score computation and top-k selection, replacing separate PyTorch operations and intermediate-memory transfers; v1 leaves GPU optimization as future work. This is a limited execution adaptation rather than a new selection algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds InfiniteBench's English multiple-choice, question-answering and summarization tasks, RULER synthetic retrieval evaluations, and PG19 examples for cache analysis in Appendix B. These materially expand the evaluated data and input types beyond the retained LongBench, L-Eval and needle-retrieval coverage.

E2.justification: InfLLM changes from a cited method in v1 to an evaluated comparator on InfiniteBench and RULER in v2 Tables 1 and 3. v2 also compares the fused kernel against its PyTorch implementation. Full-attention and StreamingLLM comparisons remain, while v1's paired Dynamic NTK multi-needle comparison is no longer reported in the corresponding v2 retrieval experiment.

E3.justification: v1 uses model-dependent cache budgets; v2 standardizes local length to 4096 and k' to 127, replacing LLaMA3's k'=96 and most other models' local length 8192/k'=256. The benchmark roster adds LLaMA3.1/3.2 and 70B/72B models while dropping LLaMA2 and InternLM2 variants. Main needle tests change from four to eight A100s and extend their length ranges. New protocols include 32K/64K/128K InfiniteBench tests, 8K/16K RULER tests and controlled attention-budget ablations.

E4.justification: v1's correct/wrong attention-distribution case study is retained as v2 Figure 8. v2 additionally tests chunk size, span size, top-k and local-window sensitivity in Table 2, examines runtime and memory scaling, and investigates synthetic-retrieval failures through cache visualizations. Appendix B expands these diagnostics across natural and synthetic texts, layers, positional encodings and models.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. The added tables and efficiency plots continue reporting point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Retained results are revised: LLaMA3's LongBench average changes from 35.07 for LongCache in v1 Table 2 to 35.03 for ReAttention in v2 Table 4, under changed cache settings. v2 adds extensive InfiniteBench, efficiency, ablation and longer-retrieval measurements. New negative findings include ReAttention's RULER MultiKey3 scores of 78.00 at 8K and 15.00 at 16K in Table 3. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not evidence of a uniform same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) retain the same mathematical operations, with only notation clarification. v2's three conditions for infinite context and its manifold-based discussion are conceptual arguments and empirical interpretations; they introduce no formal definitions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v1 claims demonstrated 400K context extension and leaves faster execution and 1M scaling to future work. v2 claims achieved million-token scaling, a 128-fold extension to 4M, and efficient execution without additional overhead. It also explicitly conditions infinite context on sufficient memory. The 4M headline attribution to LLaMA3.2 conflicts with Section 3.3 and Figure 4, which assign that result to Qwen2-1B.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive applicability limitation: poor performance on synthetic key-value retrieval, despite success on natural-context tasks. Section 4.3 and Appendix B propose disrupted cache coherence and positional ambiguity as explanations. Section 4.1 also explains semantic-fragmentation, local-context and selection-budget tradeoffs. These substantially qualify v1's predominantly favorable interpretation of position-agnostic selection.

D1.justification: Beyond revised cache settings, v2 documents the Triton operator-fusion implementation and profiling with real inference Q/K inputs on an A800-80GB GPU, a 48-core CPU and 256GB RAM. Appendix B.1 describes extracting Q/K states before and after positional embedding, reshaping them and applying t-SNE. These add implementation and analysis procedures absent from v1's evaluation settings and future optimization plan.

R1.justification: The main positioning against full-attention extrapolation and sparse retrieval methods remains. v2 sharpens its distinctions from InfLLM and LongHeads, adds RetrievalAttention and references supporting the new evaluations and analyses, and removes the xPos/parallel-context-window/NBCE discussion. This refines the existing research positioning rather than replacing it.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution statements are substantially rewritten around three conditions for infinite context and an attention-before-attention explanation. The discussion becomes three subsections, detailed benchmark reporting moves into Appendix A, and Appendix B introduces a separate diagnostic narrative. The method name, title, author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v1's two-part cache-operation diagram is replaced by a higher-level architecture diagram. Its separate benchmark tables become regrouped results in v2 Appendix Table 4 with main-text summary plots. v2 adds efficiency charts, ablation and RULER tables, and multiple t-SNE figures, while redesigning the retrieval panels. The existing attention maps are retained and relocated from Figure 4 to Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1: efficiency was previously future work, the closely related InfLLM lacked direct comparison, and hyperparameter sensitivity and synthetic-retrieval failures were unexplored. Measured efficiency, controlled ablations, additional comparisons and explicit failure analysis substantially strengthen practical validation and clarify applicability. The inconsistent attribution of the 4M result and the unproven causal interpretation of t-SNE plots weaken specific claims, but the broader evidential gains support a substantial overall improvement.
